contextNarrative: Sweden's economy has returned to positive growth territory following the 2022-2023 recession driven by high inflation and Riksbank rate rises. IMF WEO-2026-04 projects 2.1% real GDP growth for 2026, with inflation stabilising near the Riksbank's 2% target. Public finances remain strong (debt ~37% GDP, near balance). The economic recovery provides the Tidö government with macro credentials but the distributional pattern of recovery — benefiting capital and upper-income households more than lower quintiles — provides the empirical foundation for the S opposition's HD10511 interpellation strategy.

politicalEconomyLinks.link: S challenges whether 2.1% growth is broad-based; SCB Gini data (June 2026) will be decisive

disclaimers: IMF WEO values for 2025E and 2026E are projections, not actuals
